summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease, bilateral amputations, and a history of recurrent C. difficile infections was admitted for sudden-onset facial and tongue swelling, initially causing difficulty breathing. She associated the symptoms with starting mirtazipine, a new antidepressant. Evaluation revealed no airway compromise, infection, or complement deficiency, leading to a diagnosis of drug-induced angioedema. She was treated with prednisone, diphenhydramine, and famotidine in the emergency department and continued on a five-day course of prednisone. Her facial swelling resolved significantly by discharge. Management of her chronic conditions—including diabetes, C. difficile prophylaxis, dialysis, and pain—was maintained throughout. She was discharged home with instructions to discontinue mirtazipine, complete the steroid taper, and follow up with her primary and psychiatric providers.
